title: 渡荆门送别
author: 李白
intro: Sailing out of the Sichuan mountains, young Li Bai watches the hills fall away and the Yangtze spread across an endless plain. Then comes a twist: the one seeing him off is the river of his home town.
analysis: 年轻的李白坐船出了四川，经过荆门山，进入古代楚国的地方。前两句交代行程。中间两联写沿途的景色，是全诗最精彩的部分：“山随平野尽，江入大荒流”——船走出三峡，两岸的高山渐渐消失，眼前是一望无际的平原，长江在广阔的原野上奔流。“随”和“入”两个动词写出了视野由窄变宽的变化，气势非常大。接着写夜景和白天的景：月亮倒映在江中，像从天上飞下来的一面镜子；云彩变幻，结成海市蜃楼一样的楼阁。最后两句出人意料：题目说“送别”，送他的不是朋友，而是故乡的江水——江水一路流来，陪他走了万里。诗人不直接说想家，却说故乡的水舍不得他，这种把物当作人来写的拟人手法，让思乡之情显得更深、更温暖。
analysisEn: A young Li Bai sails out of Sichuan, passes Jingmen Mountain and enters the old land of Chu. The first couplet simply states the journey. The middle couplets paint what he sees, and they are the heart of the poem. “The mountains end with the level plain; the river flows into the boundless wild”: leaving the gorges behind, the high cliffs fall away and suddenly there is open plain to the horizon, with the Yangtze rolling across it. The two verbs 随 (“follow”) and 入 (“enter”) capture the view opening from narrow to vast. Then night and day: the moon’s reflection in the river looks like a mirror flying down from the sky, and the clouds pile up into towers like a mirage at sea. The ending is a surprise. The title says “farewell,” but the one seeing him off is not a friend — it is the water of his home region, which has followed him ten thousand li. Instead of saying “I miss home,” he says home misses him. Treating the river as a person makes his homesickness feel both deeper and warmer.
background: Li Bai (701–762) wrote this around 725, aged about 24, on his first journey out of Sichuan. Jingmen Mountain stands on the south bank of the Yangtze in today’s Yidu, Hubei, where the river leaves the gorges for the plain.
pronunciation: 大荒：荒 huāng。行舟：行 xíng。结海楼：结 jié。
version: 采用统编初中语文教材文本。

lines.en: I’ve sailed far, out past Jingmen,

lines.lit: I come to travel in the land of Chu.
lines.en: to roam the old country of Chu.

lines.lit: The mountains, with the level plain, come to an end;
lines.en: The mountains fade into the open plain;

lines.lit: the river enters the great wilderness and flows.
lines.en: the river rolls on into the boundless wild.

lines.lit: The moon comes down — a flying heavenly mirror;
lines.en: The moon drops in the water, a mirror flown from the sky;

lines.lit: clouds rise and form towers over the sea.
lines.en: clouds gather into towers, like a mirage at sea.

lines.lit: Still tender is the water of my home town;
lines.en: Yet it’s the water of home that loves me still —

lines.lit: for ten thousand li it sees off my travelling boat.
lines.en: it has followed my boat ten thousand miles to see me off.

words.note: 山名，在今湖北宜都长江南岸；和今天湖北的荆门市不是一个地方。
春秋战国时的国家，大致在今湖北、湖南一带；今天湖北还简称“楚”。
指一望无际的原野；今天的“荒”多是“荒凉、荒地”。
比喻倒映在江里的月亮。

words.en: towers over the sea — a mirage
words.note: 即“海市蜃楼”，今天是常用成语，比喻虚幻的东西。
古义“爱”；今天多是“可怜、怜悯”。
指从四川流来的长江水。
“舟”是船，今天说“龙舟”“同舟共济”。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 高山随着平原消失，表示诗人走出了四川的群山，眼界一下子打开。
imagery.en: The mountains vanish into the plain: the poet has left Sichuan’s ranges behind and the world suddenly opens up.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 长江奔入无边的原野，写出景色的壮阔和少年诗人的豪情。
imagery.en: The Yangtze pouring into the endless wild shows both the grand landscape and the young poet’s high spirits.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 江中月影像天上飞下的镜子，写出夜晚江面的平静明亮。
imagery.en: The moon in the river is a mirror flown down from the sky — the river at night, calm and bright.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 故乡的江水一路相送，是全诗思乡之情的落点。
imagery.en: The water of home, following him all the way, is where the poem’s homesickness finally lands.
